paragraph: The best design remains the seed, Mockingjay. Your most successful modification improved upon its parent by changing procedures.access, samplers, signatures, tables, victim.bypass_when, and introducing the new word better_bypass. Conversely, broad changes to on_fill, on_hit, victim.extremum, victim.key, and victim.tie_break resulted in significant performance drops, so you should stop altering these core replacement mechanisms. The largest remaining mistake on the traces with the most headroom (605.mcf_s-1644B, 619.lbm_s-2677B, 459.GemsFDTD-1491B, and 433.milc-127B) is wrong_bypass, meaning the policy frequently bypasses lines that are reused before any resident line. To address this, you should make victim.bypass_when more conservative, ensuring lines are inserted rather than bypassed when their predicted reuse is uncertain. On 627.cam4_s-573B, the main issue is should_bypass, while 657.xz_s-2302B suffers from kept_dead. To balance these conflicting bypass errors, focus on refining what the policy remembers in its tables and samplers, and how it decides to bypass in victim.bypass_when. A new word could be declared to express a dynamic bypass threshold that compares the incoming line's predicted reuse distance against the maximum or average predicted reuse distance of the resident lines, which the fixed vocabulary cannot easily represent.
